conviction_note: Q3 is pre-announced ($1.72-1.81, 5-10% below Q2's $1.91) and the evidence on the quarter itself (diesel climbing to a record after the 15 Sep warning, purchased-transport and driver costs still tight) leans to the lower half of the range against a $1.81 consensus at its top, while the forward evidence (diesel falling through early October so the one-week surcharge lag flips to a Q4 tailwind management already flagged, bid season opening with intermodal 30%+ cheaper than truck, US rail intermodal +6-7% y/y in late Sep/early Oct) leans positive; findings sum +1.4 but p_up only 53 because the positives are macro proxies and the moderate put skew (+4.15) and the bar at the top of the guide both point the other way, so the scaled number (+0.39) is far smaller than the sum.
bar: Company guide given 2026-09-15 at the Morgan Stanley Laguna conference: Q3 EPS down 5-10% sequentially from $1.91, i.e. $1.72-1.81, midpoint ~$1.77 (https://www.freightwaves.com/news/j-b-hunt-flags-q3-cost-pressures-shares-sink-12). Street consensus is disputed: $1.81 on 18 analysts, revenue $3.59B (https://talkbusiness.net/2026/10/j-b-hunt-q3-earnings-revenue-to-rise-analysts-say/, 2026-10-09); a Zacks-derived page shows $1.74 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/514988-what-you-need-to-know-about-jb-hunt-transport-services-incs-q3-earnings, 2026-10-15, garbled); older Zacks $1.89 after a 10.4% cut. I size against the company guide, with $1.81 as the headline number the wire will compare to. print_vs_bar_pct is EPS ~$1.77 vs $1.81 = about -2%; revenue likely above $3.59B on record fuel surcharge.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest via Equibles: 3,227,884 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up 1.19M (+58%) from 2,036,176 on 2026-09-15, about 3.4% of 93.9M shares outstanding, 2.10 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/jbht/shortinterest). Shorts added after the warning but this is not crowded. Baseline: 25-delta skew +4.15 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 1.02, front-week straddle 5.75% against a 7.38% median of the last 7 reactions (4 up, 3 down; +8.0 and +6.3 on the last two beats, +22.1 on Q3 2025). Spot $233.90, -21.6% from the 52-week high, +2.4% over 5 days, -1.2% over 20; the stock fell ~9-12% on the 2026-09-16 warning.

findings.finding: US diesel kept rising after J.B. Hunt gave its 15 Sep guide: the national average was about $5.97-6.06 around 9-11 Sep, a record $6.44 on 18 Sep and $6.505-6.51 on 21 Sep (vs $3.70 a year earlier), and still about $6.45 on 28 Sep. With a one-week surcharge lag, the last two weeks of Q3 carried more fuel headwind than the 'at least $10M' cited at the conference, against a consensus of $1.81 that already sits at the TOP of the $1.72-1.81 guide. That points to EPS in the lower half and a headline miss against $1.81.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The intra-quarter warning that cited fuel and driver costs took the stock down ~9-12% on 2026-09-16. EPS beats on the last two prints were bought: +8.0% (Q2 2026, $1.91 vs $1.71) and +6.3% (Q1 2026). This quarter has no history of a print landing inside a pre-announced range.
findings.why_not_priced: The diesel series is public, but the sell-side has not marked consensus down to the guide midpoint ($1.81 is the top of the range, and older Zacks numbers sit at $1.89). If the market had priced a lower-half print, consensus would read about $1.75-1.77. The finding lands inside the company's guided range, so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Peak of $6.505 on 21 Sep (AAA/GasBuddy, aggregated in search; record crossing on 2026-09-11 at https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/11/texas-california-and-26-other-states-hit-record-high-diesel-prices-as-diesel-passes-6-a-gallon-for-the-first-time-ever/). FreightWaves on the warning says diesel 'kept climbing through September' and that surcharges lag one week (https://www.freightwaves.com/news/j-b-hunt-flags-q3-cost-pressures-shares-sink-12). The cost estimate is a proxy calculation, not a company number.

findings.finding: Diesel turned down after quarter-end: GasBuddy reported the US national average down 14.2 cents in the week to 5 Oct, to $6.307, falling in 48 states, and about $6.25 by 11 Oct, from the $6.51 peak on 21 Sep. At the conference management said the fuel-surcharge lag 'should reverse into a tailwind when prices fall'. So the Q4 commentary on the call can describe fuel flipping from a Q3 headwind of at least $10M to a Q4 tailwind. The market's Q4 bar was set during the warning, while diesel was still rising.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: J.B. Hunt gives no formal EPS guidance. The stock trades on call commentary about the next quarter: +22.1% on Q3 2025, and +8.0% on Q2 2026 when management talked up conversion and bid-season pricing. -7.7% and -7.4% on the early-2025 prints when the outlook was cautious.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is $234 against ~$226 on 8 Oct and ~$255 before the warning, so it has recovered only a small part of the warning drop. If the market expected the fuel headwind to reverse, the stock would have recovered more of that drop and consensus would not have been cut. Most of the warning was attributed to fuel and driver costs, and fuel is now reversing.
findings.independence: Company statement that the lag reverses: https://www.freightwaves.com/news/j-b-hunt-flags-q3-cost-pressures-shares-sink-12 (2026-09-16). European diesel also fell in early October, e.g. Germany to EUR 2.25/l on 5 Oct (https://www.fuel-prices.eu/news/germany-diesel-below-2-40-eur-2026-10-05/). The GasBuddy figure is a secondhand forum quote, so this is a macro proxy.

findings.finding: US rail intermodal volume, the industry series for JBHT's largest segment (intermodal plus dedicated are 96% of operating income), ran +6.3% y/y in the week to 26 Sep, +6.9% to 19 Sep and +7.4% in the week to 3 Oct, against +4.2% YTD. In Q2 J.B. Hunt grew intermodal loads 10% against 8% for the Class Is, and June was +12%. That points to another record intermodal load quarter in Q3, above 578k, and a strong early-October run-rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Record intermodal volume (+10%) with an EPS beat bought +8.0% on Q2 2026. The intermodal volume rebound bought +22.1% on Q3 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: Management already called demand 'really strong' at the conference, so volume strength is largely expected. Volume is not the line the warning hit. What is not visible yet is the size of JBHT's outperformance in Q3. This is an industry proxy and sized small.
findings.independence: Weekly AAR prints for 19 and 26 Sep (+6.9%, +6.3%): https://www.ajot.com/news/aar-reports-rail-traffic-for-the-week-ending-september-26-2026. Q2 outperformance vs Class Is: https://www.freightwaves.com/?p=575743 (2026-07-16).

findings.finding: Intermodal bid season opens in October with about 10% of contracts renewing in Q4. Market evidence points to pricing power: SONAR's National Truckload Index was $3.53/mile on about 1 Oct, ~50% above a year ago and >10% above the late-August low; dry van tender rejections were 13.8%, more than double the 5-7% balanced range; truck-to-intermodal spread above 30%. Management said in July it would raise contractual intermodal rates this bid season. The Q3 call is the first place they can quantify early bid-season wins, which the market has not seen.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pricing and conversion commentary helped the +8.0% (Q2 2026) and +22.1% (Q3 2025) moves. Early-2025 bid seasons with 'mixed results' and only 'modest success' repairing rates coincided with the -7.7% and -7.4% prints.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-01 (date from SONAR readings cited in the article; year confirmed by the 2026 cycle context)
findings.why_not_priced: Stephens and others frame the spread as a 12-18 month story and cut targets. The sell-side has not put Q4 intermodal yield into its numbers, consistent with revisions that are still falling (current-year EPS -6.8% over the last month per AAII). One risk the size allows for: management has said it will not impose out-of-cycle rate hikes, and most renewals fall in Q1-Q3 2027, so the call may defer the payoff.
findings.independence: Management's July plan to raise rates in bid season: https://www.freightwaves.com/?p=575743. The >30% spread was reiterated in September: https://www.freightwaves.com/news/j-b-hunt-flags-q3-cost-pressures-shares-sink-12. Stephens' 30%+ spread view: https://talkbusiness.net/2026/10/j-b-hunt-q3-earnings-revenue-to-rise-analysts-say/. All three are partly the company's own framing.

findings.finding: Cost pressure on the asset-light and truck lines did not ease after the warning. Management said capacity is 'not letting up at all' and may be getting worse, and that purchased-transportation spot costs rose up to 30% within the quarter. SONAR spot rates kept climbing into October (NTI $3.53/mi). In Q2, Truckload (JBT) gross profit already fell 12% on third-party capacity costs and ICS gross margin was 12.5% vs 15.5% a year earlier. Q3 margins in ICS and JBT, and Dedicated driver costs ($25M of driver-related cost added sequentially), are the risk to the quarter and to the Q4 cost commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-09-16 cost warning cost ~9-12% in one session. The Q2 beat came despite JBT gross profit -12% and was bought +8%, so these smaller segments have not driven the stock when intermodal was strong.
findings.why_not_priced: Most of this is inside the guide the company gave on 15 Sep, so it is sized near zero. What is unpriced is any further deterioration in the last two weeks of September, when spot rates kept rising. Net of the rest of the company: ICS plus JBT are ~18% of revenue and a small share of operating income, while intermodal plus dedicated carry 96%.
findings.independence: Q2 segment detail: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/22/jb-hunt-jbht-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/. SONAR spot rates: https://www.freightwaves.com/news/spot-rates-split-as-tender-rejections-hold-above-13. This shares the 15 Sep conference as a source with the first finding, but rests on a different cost line (purchased transportation and drivers, not fuel).

findings.finding: Positioning after the warning leans short but is not crowded. Short interest rose 58% to 3.23M shares (3.4% of shares outstanding, 2.1 days to cover) at the 30 Sep settlement. The stock is -21.6% from its 52-week high, and Citizens upgraded to Outperform ($300 PT) after the pullback, while UBS ($264) and Raymond James ($300) cut targets. Q3 EPS is pre-announced, so a print inside the range removes uncertainty, and the shorts added after the warning are the marginal buyers if the Q4 commentary is constructive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print inside a pre-announced range for this name in the baseline. Moderately positioned name, median absolute reaction 7.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: The put skew of +4.15 vol points says the options market is paying for downside, which is the opposite of what a market positioned for a relief rally would show. At 2.1 days to cover the squeeze is a weak mechanism, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Citizens upgrade after the pullback: https://tradersunion.com/news/financial-news/show/3368757-jb-hunt-upgrade-after-pullback/. UBS/RJ target cuts of 2026-09-17 via Benzinga summary (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/JBHT/price-targets).

outside_window.finding: Most intermodal contract repricing from this bid season lands in Q1-Q3 2027 (only ~10% of contracts renew in Q4), so the earnings payoff from the >30% truck-intermodal spread is mostly after the window. Only the call commentary on it is inside the window and that is filed above.
Knight-Swift reports Q3 on 2026-10-21 after the close, after this window. Its truckload read-across cannot reach this trade.

baseline_tension: The forward-looking findings lean against the moderate put skew (+4.15) and the bar at the top of the guide. My reason the options market may be wrong: the quarter itself is pre-announced, and since the warning the main warned cost (fuel) has turned. That is a macro proxy, not a company number, so p_up moves only to 53.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): both reported-quarter cost findings land inside the company's $1.72-1.81 range. Fuel -0.8 -> -0.4, purchased transport/driver -0.6 -> -0.3.

Rule 5 (proxy vs company number): the diesel-reversal, AAR volume and bid-season findings rest on industry series, not company numbers. Diesel reversal +1.0 -> +0.8, AAR volume +0.6 -> +0.4, bid season +0.8 -> +0.6.
Rule 7 (sign against skew): the net positive lean runs against +4.15 skew, so p_up 54 -> 53 and the reason is written in baseline_tension.
Rule 6 (bar): consensus is disputed ($1.74/$1.81/$1.89), but the company guide supplies a sourceable bar, so no blanket cap was applied.
Positioning finding (+0.3) unchanged: short interest was checked and is not crowded.
